newsitem.title: UK: Dalgety warns on profits as charges soar.
newsitem.headline: Dalgety warns on profits as charges soar.

text.p: British foods and agricultural feeds business Dalgety Plc said on Tuesday full-year profits would be lower than expected because of poor fourth-quarter trading and higher exceptional charges.

Dalgety said exceptional charges, which it earlier forecast at 36 million pounds ($60.6 million), were now expected to total 138 million. Dalgety said it now expected pre-tax profit for the year of not less than 65 million pounds.

"These results are unacceptable and shareholder value must be restored. Extensive management actions will produce benefits that will become increasingly apparent during 1997/98 and beyond. In addition, the board is undertaking a fundamental and rapid reappraisal of the group's businesses," chairman Denys Henderson said.

Dalgety said fourth quarter trading in agriculture was disappointing, with the performance at the arable supply business below earlier expectations because of low-priced fertiliser imports and the wettest June on record in Britain.

Dalgety, which reiterated its earlier forecast that expected to pay a final dividend of at least six pence per share, said exceptional costs for its petfoods division had now more than doubled to 67 million pounds.

But Dalgety said it had brought the production problems outlined in May at its petfoods business under control and progress had been made in cutting costs. It said it now expected to save 20 million pounds per annum compared with 12 million earlier and also pledged a substantial recovery in profits at both its agriculture and petfoods businesses.
